requirements.evidence: Two open bins bin:0,0,0~hex-bin-full and bin:1,0,0~hex-bin-full on pieces 0,0,0 and 1,0,0 provide two compartments for utensils; staged with spoon (prop:4), fork (prop:5) in bin 1 and knife (prop:6) in bin 2, visible in look az30 polar62.
Exactly two bin parts placed: bin:0,0,0~hex-bin-full and bin:1,0,0~hex-bin-full (counts bin:2). Capped and locked build, meshClash clear.

Configurator checks fit/collisions only and cannot verify waterproofing. Parts are 3D-printed and material/print choice determines water-tightness; layer lines and joints may leak. No seal validated. Do not assume waterproof.

Dishwasher safety depends on material, heat/chemical resistance chosen by user, which configurator does not check. 3D-printed plastic may warp or degrade in dishwasher; not verified. Recommend hand-wash unless printed in certified dishwasher-safe material.

finish.summary: Built a compact two-cell utensil holder with two full-depth bins and staged with spoon/fork/knife to show use. Geometry for two bins is met and verified (check_build ok, mesh clear). Waterproof and dishwasher-safe claims cannot be met by configurator alone — they depend on filament/material and print settings outside this system, so marked unmet with safe-use guidance.

lines.label: M6 x 25 socket head screw, ISO 4762

notes: Tighten every M6 to 2 N.m: HAND TOOLS ONLY, never a cordless driver. These bolts clamp printed PETG, not metal: at the bolt's own 10.4 N.m rating the head crushes the plastic under it and the joint fails silently, looking tight while holding nothing. Snug, then a nudge. Re-check the bolts after the first few weeks: PETG relaxes under load and the clamp will have eased.
